title: Ambient completion presentations for integral pullback and tensor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=A/t^nA$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale site of each $W=X,Y$, put $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use $D(R_W)$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F_f:D(R_Y)\to D(R_X)$ be ordinary ambient derived module pullback along the canonical ring map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$, induced by the finite quotient projections [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Put
$$C_WQ=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(Q\otimes_{R_W}^{\mathbf L}(A_n)_W),$$
with its quotient augmentation and strict-tower derived limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Let $\widehat F_f$ and $\widehat T_W$ be precisely the finite-quotient definitions of integral pullback and completed tensor in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Then for all $K\in D(R_Y)$ and $M,N\in D(R_W)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$C_XF_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat F_fK,\qquad C_W(M\otimes_{R_W}^{\mathbf L}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat T_W(M,N).$$
On flat-term K-flat representatives $P\to K$ and $U\to M,V\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], these are the derived limits of the isomorphisms of entire strict towers
$$(f^*P)\otimes_{R_X}(A_n)_X\cong f_n^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_n)_Y),$$
$$\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_{R_W}V)\otimes_{R_W}(A_n)_W\cong\operatorname{Tot}((U\otimes_{R_W}(A_n)_W)\otimes_{(A_n)_W}(V\otimes_{R_W}(A_n)_W)),$$
where $\operatorname{Tot}$ is the direct-sum total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].
The maps are the balanced tensor associativity maps and identify the quotient augmentations with the defining operation augmentations, including their zero shifted-product component. They commute with all quotient transitions and with changes of the K-flat representatives. No identification $f^{-1}R_Y=R_X$ and no completeness or constructibility assumption is required.

proof.text: Write $S_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$, $\pi_{W,n}:R_W\to S_{W,n}$, and $\rho_{W,n}:S_{W,n+1}\to S_{W,n}$. Let $c_n:f^{-1}S_{Y,n}\to S_{X,n}$ be the constant-coefficient structure maps. They commute with $\rho_n$: both composites send a constant section $a$ to its image modulo $t^n$, and sheafification determines the maps. The maps $c_nf^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$ therefore form a cone. The limit universal property of $R_X$ defines $c:f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ with $\pi_{X,n}c=c_nf^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$. Thus the coefficient square at each $n$ commutes. This construction uses inverse image on the projections and then the universal property on $X$; it never interchanges inverse image with an inverse limit.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; constant-section structure maps and limit cone

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to K$, $U\to M$, $V\to N$. The ambient pullback $F_fK$ is represented by $f^*P$, which is itself K-flat with flat terms. Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_{R_W}V)$; this is a flat-term K-flat representative of $M\otimes^L_{R_W}N$. Hence the strict completion towers of these two ambient objects are represented, without any additional resolutions depending on $n$, by $(f^*P)\otimes_{R_X}S_{X,n}$ and $T\otimes_{R_W}S_{W,n}$. This follows by computing derived scalar extension on a K-flat complex. All these assertions hold for unbounded complexes.

Apply the ordinary scalar-association isomorphism $\kappa$ for the coefficient square of Step 1. Its inverse gives, degreewise, an $S_{X,n}$-linear isomorphism
$$b_n:(f^*P)\otimes_{R_X}S_{X,n}\longrightarrow f_n^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{Y,n}).$$
With the scalar written first, its formula on local generalized generators is
$$(r\otimes x)\otimes a\longmapsto \pi_{X,n}(r)a\otimes(x\otimes1),$$
and its inverse sends $a\otimes(x\otimes b)$ to $(1\otimes x)\otimes a c_n(b)$, where $b$ is a section of $f^{-1}S_{Y,n}$. These are the normalized $\kappa$ and its inverse, not maps using an identification of the completed rings. The commuting coefficient square is precisely the balancing relation needed for these formulas. Since they commute with the differential of $P$, they give chain isomorphisms natural in chain maps $P\to P'$.

The existing strict tensor-reduction comparison applies to $U,V$ on $W$. Its normalized degree-$(p,q)$ constituent can be written
$$d_n:(x\otimes y)\otimes a\longmapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1),$$
with inverse $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. Balancing makes both formulas well defined and their two composites the identity. The sheaf-tensor universal property extends these formulas from bilinear local generators. Scalar extension preserves the direct sums over $p+q=i$, so these constituents define the displayed total-complex isomorphism. The differential calculation on both sides is $dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$, with unchanged coefficient $a$; thus no boundedness or rearrangement of infinite products is involved.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, scalar-extension formula; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, homogeneous total tensor calculation

proof.text: The maps in Steps 3–4 are isomorphisms of whole strict towers, not merely isomorphisms of their evaluated objects in a derived category. Indeed, applying $\rho_{X,n}$ before or after $b$ sends $(r\otimes x)\otimes a$ to $\pi_{X,n}(r)\rho_{X,n}(a)\otimes(x\otimes1)$. Compatibility of the $c_n$ with reduction gives the same value when the source coefficient of $P_{n+1}$ is reduced first. For $d$, the two paths send $(x\otimes y)\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes\rho_{W,n}(a))\otimes(y\otimes1)$. Linearity, balancing and the universal property give equality on sheaves in every degree. Adjacent transition equations imply all $m\to n$ equations by composition. Because $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$, these are equations of $R_X$- or $R_W$-linear maps after restriction of scalars.

source.place: Tag 03EK, tensor universal property and the scalar-extension formula; explicit quotient transition calculation

proof.text: The right-hand towers are the finite-operation towers in the stated definitions: $P_n,U_n,V_n$ are flat-term K-flat over $S_n$ by change of rings, so $f_n^*P_n$ computes $L(f_n)^*K_n$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes_{S_n}V_n)$ computes $M_n\otimes^L_{S_n}N_n$. The natural comparisons for ambient pullback and total tensor therefore identify the left towers with the completion towers of Step 2 and the right towers with those defining $\widehat F_fK$ and $\widehat T_W(M,N)$. Restriction of scalars is exact, so it does not change these quasi-isomorphism computations.

Apply the functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))\to D(R)$ to the strict isomorphisms of Step 5. A functor carries an isomorphism and its inverse to mutually inverse maps. Step 6 identifies the resulting sources and targets as $C_XF_fK,\widehat F_fK$ and $C_W(M\otimes^L_{R_W}N),\widehat T_W(M,N)$, respectively. This produces both asserted isomorphisms by the strict-tower derived-limit functor, rather than by choosing morphisms between abstract Roos triangles.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; derived functor on strict towers

proof.text: Check the augmentations before taking limits. For pullback, the quotient map is $f^*P\to(f^*P)\otimes S_{X,n}$, $r\otimes x\mapsto(r\otimes x)\otimes1$; under $b_n$ it becomes $\pi_{X,n}(r)\otimes(x\otimes1)$, exactly scalar insertion into $f_n^*P_n$. For tensor, $x\otimes y\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes1$ becomes $(x\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes1)$ under $d_n$, the defining finite tensor augmentation. These are compatible families by Step 5. In the strict Roos coordinates consisting of the shifted-product coordinate followed by the unshifted-product coordinate, the associated chain augmentation is $z\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nz)_n)$. A strict tower map acts by the same product map diagonally on both coordinates, hence carries this augmentation to $(0,(b_n\gamma_nz)_n)$, or the expression with $d_n$. In particular the shifted-product component remains zero.

source.place: Tag 0941, proof: explicit shifted cone coordinates and strict augmentations

proof.text: Countable products of $R_W$-module sheaves on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact. The strict Roos derivation theorem therefore identifies the localized functorial cone model with total right derived inverse limit, compatibly with its ordinary-limit inclusion. Apply it to the augmented towers of Step 8: their cone maps are exactly the representatives of the maps obtained in Step 7. Thus the augmentation equalities hold for the specified derived limits as well as for their cone representatives. Choose all small-site and localization universes inside a single larger universe, as permitted by the small-site convention; the theorem's size and sheafification hypotheses are then the usual module-sheaf hypotheses. No product-preservation assertion for $f^{-1}$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, strict naturality refinement; exact pro-etale products as recorded in the cited node

proof.text: Every formula above is natural in chain maps of the chosen flat-term K-flat representatives. The derived pullback and scalar-extension comparisons are natural in maps of resolutions; the finite operations descend independently of resolutions. For completeness, on a quasi-isomorphism between such representatives the ambient pullback, scalar-extension towers and finite-operation towers all give invertible maps after localization by the cited results. The commuting naturality square for that chain map therefore also commutes for its inverse: multiply the square by the inverse maps on both sides. Quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category admit a right calculus of fractions. The full subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes resolves every complex by Step 2; the functor from complexes to the homotopy category is full and surjective on objects. The resolving-representative restriction theorem therefore descends the comparison uniquely (using an unused second variable for the unary case). Its hypotheses are exactly these resolution and fraction properties. It follows that both comparisons descend naturally to all derived morphisms and commute with the canonical changes of resolutions. This argument also applies with both tensor variables varying. Step 8's strict naturality gives the same conclusion for the augmentation equalities. No completeness, constructibility, or cohomological boundedness was used.
